sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *se* with a verb from B1 Unit 6. It leaves out who does the action, which is useful when a text speaks of cuts, taxes and agreements and the decision-makers stay in the background. With no noun the verb stays singular; with a noun the verb agrees with it.

items.spanish: Se recortó el gasto público en muchos países.
items.english: Public spending was cut in many countries.

items.spanish: Se pedía a los gobiernos exportar más.
items.english: Governments were asked to export more.

items.spanish: En esos años se trabajaba más y se ganaba menos.
items.english: In those years people worked more and earned less.

sections.content: Singular noun, singular verb (*se recortó el gasto*); plural noun, plural verb (*se subieron los impuestos*); no noun, singular verb (*se trabajaba más*). Use *se* when the agent is unknown or not important; if you want to name the agent, use an active sentence: *el FMI pidió recortes*.
